name: triage

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    name: Triage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Welcome contributor and label pull request
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
        with:
          script: |
            const pullRequest = context.payload.pull_request;

            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: pullRequest.number,
              body: `Welcome, @${pullRequest.user.login}! Thanks for opening "${pullRequest.title}".`,
            });

            await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: pullRequest.number,
              labels: ["needs-triage"],
            });

## Contributing

Open a pull request. Contributions arrive from forks.

## Workflows

- `ci.yml` runs the test suite on every pull request.
- `triage.yml` runs when a pull request is opened, including from forks. It comments a welcome
  message that includes the contributor's username and the pull request title, and it applies the
  `needs-triage` label. It uses `pull_request_target` (for a write-scoped token against fork PRs)
  without checking out the pull request's code.

content.text: Now let me verify the workflow YAML is valid and double-check the label needs to pre-exist (it doesn't — GitHub creates ad hoc labels via `addLabels` only if they already exist; otherwise it 404s). Let me confirm that behavior.

Created `.github/workflows/triage.yml` (fires on `pull_request_target: opened`, permissions restricted to `pull-requests: write`, no checkout of PR code so fork contributions can't run arbitrary code with the write-scoped token) and updated `README.md` with a Workflows section documenting it.

Files changed:
- `.github/workflows/triage.yml` (new)
- `README.md`

Note on the fork-safety design: I used `pull_request_target` instead of `pull_request` because the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` for `pull_request` events from forks is read-only and can't post comments or add labels. `pull_request_target` runs with a write-scoped token in the base repo's context, which is safe here specifically because the job never checks out or executes the fork's code — it only reads `context.payload.pull_request` fields (title, username) inside the trusted `github-script` step, so there's no way for a malicious PR title/branch to inject into a shell command or get executed.
